about: Reference list /grammar/verbs-with-prepositions (English: verbs with prepositions). items: [verb + preposition, what follows (sb = somebody, sth = something), example, level]. Sorted by preposition; a section's name is the preposition itself (the worksheet blanks it in the example, so each example uses it once, as the verb's preposition, before any other use).
title: Verbs with prepositions
metaTitle: Verbs with prepositions: list with examples – Reference – icanspeak Spanish
description: Common English verbs with a fixed preposition, sorted by preposition from about to with: what follows each one, and an example sentence.
lead: The most common verbs with a fixed preposition, sorted from about to with. For each verb: what follows it and an example.
regel: Learn the verb and its preposition together: *wait for, listen to, depend on.*
After a preposition use a noun, a pronoun or the -ing form: *I'm thinking about moving.* (not *about to move*)
In questions the preposition usually goes to the end: *Who are you waiting for? What are you looking at?*
Some verbs take no preposition, even if your language uses one: *discuss the plan* (not *discuss about*), *phone Tom, marry Tom, enter the room.*
A different preposition can change the meaning: *look at* (see), *look for* (try to find), *look after* (take care of).
practice: Prepositions at the end of a question

sections.name: about
items: I'm thinking about moving to Bristol.
He really cares about his students.

sections.name: at
items: We arrived at the hotel late.
Why are you laughing at me?

sections.name: for
items: Can I ask for the bill?
I apologise for being late. (US: apologize)

sections.name: from
items: Can I borrow some money from you?
It took weeks to recover from the flu.

sections.name: in
items: We arrived in London at six.
Fifty runners took part in the race.
She succeeded in passing the exam.
The shop specialises in old maps. (US: specialize)

sections.name: of
items: What do you think of my new haircut?
The team consists of five people.
She dreams of living by the sea.
My parents don't approve of my plans.

sections.name: on
items: I spend too much on clothes.
I can't concentrate on my work.
We congratulated her on her new job.

sections.name: to
items: I listen to the radio in the car.
Can you explain the rule to me?
You should apologise to your sister.

sections.name: with
items: Can you help me with my homework?
I share a flat with two friends.
He often argues with his brother.
